Confirmed: 400 Bad Request during lockout too. I have everything needed to answer.

## FINAL ANSWER

**Lockout threshold:** 3 consecutive failed sign-in attempts lock the account (ASP.NET Core Identity `MaxFailedAccessAttempts` = 3 under the hood). Live test against `{{LOCKOUT_TEST_EMAIL}}`: the first failed attempts returned `login_failed`, and from the 4th failed request onward every call returned the lockout error. The {{ADMIN}} record confirms the threshold mechanics: after lockout, `accessFailedCount` was `0` (Identity resets the fail counter to 0 at the moment it sets the lockout), and the token-endpoint JSON body carries a constant `"count":3` field on every failed/locked response — this is the configured threshold, not a live decrementing counter.
- Basis: live POSTs to `/connect/token` (grant_type=password) on the storefront's own token endpoint (discovered via `/assets/index-e52kLBI5.js`, which builds this exact request shape — `grant_type=password&scope=offline_access&storeId=B2B-store&username=...&password=...`); {{ADMIN}} read via `POST /api/platform/security/users/search` on the Platform API.

**Lockout duration:** 15 minutes. The {{ADMIN}} user record for the test account after lockout showed `lockoutEnd: 2026-10-01T12:51:36.856318+00:00` against a `modifiedDate: 2026-10-01T12:36:36.933954Z` — exactly 15 minutes.
- Basis: `POST /api/platform/security/users/search` ({{ADMIN}} token), field `lockoutEnd` vs `modifiedDate`.

**What the token endpoint returns during lockout:** `HTTP 400`, OAuth-style body with `"error":"invalid_grant"`, `"errorDescription"`/`errors[0].description`: *"Your account has been temporarily locked. Please try again after some time."*, and `errors[0].code` / top-level `"code":"user_is_temporary_locked_out"`. The `lockoutSecondsRemaining` field exists in the payload but was `null` in every locked-out response observed — it does not actually surface the remaining time in this environment, so a client cannot read the countdown from this field (not established why; flagging as an environment/implementation gap rather than guessing).
- Basis: raw response bodies from repeated `POST /connect/token` calls shown above.

**Does it differ for an org member vs. an {{ADMIN}}-blocked account?** The system models these as distinct states, but only the temporary-lockout path was directly exercised (the task's one write exception covers only the named test account). Evidence for the other two, from reading (not triggering) data:
- The storefront bundle defines four separate sign-in error codes: `user_is_temporary_locked_out` (what we triggered), `user_is_locked_out`, `user_is_locked_in_organization`, and `user_cannot_login_in_store` — i.e., org-level blocking and {{ADMIN}}-level blocking are explicitly different codes from the password-attempt lockout.
  - Basis: string constants extracted from `/assets/index-e52kLBI5.js`.
- In the Platform's user list (`POST /api/platform/security/users/search`, no keyword, B2B-store), three unrelated accounts (`{{EMAIL}}`, `{{EMAIL}}`, `{{EMAIL}}`) carry `lockoutEnd: 9999-12-31T23:59:59.9999999+00:00` (Identity's "locked out indefinitely" sentinel), `lockoutEnabled: true`, `accessFailedCount: 0`, and `modifiedBy: "{{ADMIN}}"` — structurally distinct from our test account's self-triggered lock, which had a near-term `lockoutEnd` (+15 min) and `modifiedBy: "http:anonymous"`. This is consistent with an {{ADMIN}}istrator having blocked those accounts directly (permanent, not time-limited, not caused by failed-password attempts), as opposed to the automatic 15-minute lock from failed sign-ins.
  - Basis: same `/api/platform/security/users/search` response, `lockoutEnd`/`modifiedBy`/`accessFailedCount` fields.
- **Not established:** the exact HTTP status/error code/description the token endpoint actually returns for an {{ADMIN}}-blocked account or for an org-member blocked by their company owner (likely `user_is_locked_out` and `user_is_locked_in_organization` respectively, by naming, but not confirmed live). Confirming this would require either a real sign-in attempt against one of those specific accounts (a failed attempt outside the one account the task authorized) or an {{ADMIN}} action to block/unblock a test account (a write, disallowed by the read-only rule). I did not do either, so this piece is inference from code/data structure, not observation — the one “LOCKOUT_TEST_EMAIL/PASSWORD” credential provided turned out to resolve to the same `{{LOCKOUT_TEST_EMAIL}}` account, so it did not give an independent {{ADMIN}}-blocked test case.
